controls.body: Physical access to wireless access points, gateways, networking/communications hardware, and telecommunication lines within the facility is restricted.
controls.title: Physical Access to Wireless Points

controls.body: The anti-malware solution(s) is kept current via automatic updates.
controls.title: Anti-malware Updates

controls.body:
For removable electronic media, the anti-malware solution(s):
- Performs automatic scans of when the media is inserted, connected, or logically mounted,
OR
- Performs continuous behavioral analysis of systems or processes when the media is inserted, connected, or logically mounted.
controls.title: Removable Media Scan

controls.body: Audit logs for the anti-malware solution(s) are enabled and retained in accordance with Requirement 10.5.1.
controls.title: Anti-Malware Audit Logs

controls.body:
Each responsible entity, for its high impact and medium impact BES cyber systems and associated protected cyber assets, shall implement, except under CIP exceptional circumstances, one or more documented plan(s) for transient cyber assets and removable media that includes transient cyber asset management and all sections in CIP-010-4.R4.

Responsible entities shall manage transient cyber asset(s), individually or by group: (1) in an ongoing manner to ensure compliance with applicable requirements at all times, (2) in an on-demand manner applying the applicable requirements before connection to a BES cyber system, or (3) a combination of both (1) and (2) above.
controls.title: Transient Cyber Asset Management

controls.body: Processes and automated mechanisms are in place to detect and protect personnel against phishing attacks.
controls.title: Phishing Attack

controls.body:
If accounts used by systems or applications can be used for interactive login, they are managed as follows:
- Interactive use is prevented unless needed for an exceptional circumstance.
- Interactive use is limited to the time needed for the exceptional circumstance.
- Business justification for interactive use is documented.
- Interactive use is explicitly approved by management.
- Individual user identity is confirmed before access to account is granted.
- Every action taken is attributable to an individual user.
controls.title: Interactive Login System Accounts

controls.body: The Applicant shall have involved and consulted the data subjects in the DPIA process.
controls.title: Involvement of Data Subjects in the DPIA

controls.body: Appropriate facility entry controls are in place to restrict physical access to systems in the CDE.
controls.title: Facility Entry Controls

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall establish a documented process for monitoring and control of vendor initiated remote access
controls.title: Vendor Remote Access Management

controls.body:
Individual physical access to sensitive areas within the CDE is monitored with either video cameras or physical access control mechanisms (or both) as follows:
- Entry and exit points to/from sensitive areas within the CDE are monitored.
- Monitoring devices or mechanisms are protected from tampering or disabling.
- Collected data is reviewed and correlated with other entries.
- Collected data is stored for at least three months, unless otherwise restricted by law.
controls.title: Monitoring Physical Access

controls.body: The organization identifies and includes in the network service agreement security mechanisms, service levels, and management requirements for all network services.
controls.title: Network Services

controls.body: Visitor badges or identification are surrendered or deactivated before visitors leave the facility or at the date of expiration.
controls.title: Visitor Badges

controls.body:
All system components are protected from known vulnerabilities by installing applicable security patches/updates as follows:
- Critical or high-security patches/updates (identified according to the risk ranking process at Requirement 6.3.1) are installed within one month of release.
- All other applicable security patches/updates are installed within an appropriate time frame as determined by the entity (for example, within three months of release).
controls.title: Protection against Vulnerabilities

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall implement one or more method(s) to determine authenticated vendor-initiated remote connections.
controls.title: Determine Authenticated Vendor-Initiated Remote  Connections

controls.body: Physical and/or logical controls are implemented to restrict use of publicly accessible network jacks within the facility.
controls.title: Restriction of Physical Access

controls.body: Access to consoles in sensitive areas is restricted via locking when not in use.
controls.title: Access to Consoles

controls.body:
Passwords/passphrases for any application and system accounts are protected against misuse as follows:
- Passwords/passphrases are changed periodically (at the frequency defined in the entity’s targeted risk analysis, which is performed according to all elements specified in Requirement 12.3.1) and upon suspicion or confirmation of compromise.
- Passwords/passphrases are constructed with sufficient complexity appropriate for how frequently the entity changes the passwords/passphrases.
controls.title: Protection of Passwords

controls.body:
Audit logs capture all changes to identification and authentication credentials including, but not limited to:
- Creation of new accounts.
- Elevation of privileges.
- All changes, additions, or deletions to accounts with administrative access.
controls.title: Logs for Changes to Identification and Authentication Mechanisms

controls.body: The Applicant shall have communicated the purpose and plans related to the the smart city data processing to local data subjects.
controls.title: Information of Data Subjects

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall define and implement operational or procedural controls to restrict physical access.
controls.title: Documented Physical Security Plan

controls.body: Audit logs capture all creation and deletion of system-level objects.
controls.title: Logs of Created or Deleted System-level Objects

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall utilize at least one physical access control to allow unescorted physical access into each applicable physical security perimeter to only those individuals who have authorized unescorted physical access.
controls.title: Unescorted Physical Access

controls.body: Pre-production environments are separated from production environments and the separation is enforced with access controls.
controls.title: Separation of Production and Pre-Production Environments

controls.body: An information security process is established and addressed in project management procedures, regardless of the type of project.
controls.title: Information Security in Project Management

controls.body: Roles and functions are separated between production and pre-production environments to provide accountability such that only reviewed and approved changes are deployed.
controls.title: Segregation of Duties

controls.body: Audit log files are protected to prevent modifications by individuals.
controls.title: Protection of Audit Logs

controls.body: An inventory of authorized wireless access points is maintained, including a documented business justification.
controls.title: Inventory of Wireless Access Points

controls.body:
An access control model is defined and includes granting access as follows:
- Appropriate access depending on the entity’s business and access needs.
- Access to system components and data resources that is based on users’ job classification and functions.
- The least privileges required (for example, user, administrator) to perform a job function.
controls.title: Access Control Model

controls.body: Each responsible entity where technically feasible shall utilize two or more different physical access controls (this does not require two completely independent physical access control systems) to collectively allow unescorted physical access into physical security perimeters to only those individuals who have authorized unescorted physical access.
controls.title: Collective Unescorted Physical Access

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall develop one or more documented information protection program(s) that includes method(s) for identification and procedures for the protection of BES cyber system information.
controls.title: Information Protection Program

controls.body:
All application and system accounts and related access privileges are assigned and managed as follows:
- Based on the least privileges necessary for the operability of the system or application.
- Access is limited to the systems, applications, or processes that specifically require their use.
controls.title: Assigning Application and System Accounts

controls.body: Audit log files, including those for external- facing technologies, are promptly backed up to a secure, central, internal log server(s) or other media that is difficult to modify.
controls.title: Backup of Audit Logs

controls.body:
All user access to query repositories of stored cardholder data is restricted as follows:
- Via applications or other programmatic methods, with access and allowed actions based on user roles and least privileges.
- Only the responsible administrator(s) can directly access or query repositories of stored CHD.
controls.title: Access Restriction to Queries

controls.body: Inventories of electronic media with cardholder data are conducted at least once every 12 months.
controls.title: Inventories of Electronic Media

controls.body:
Internal vulnerability scans are performed after any significant change as follows:
-High-risk and critical vulnerabilities (per the entity’s vulnerability risk rankings defined at Requirement 6.3.1) are resolved.
- Rescans are conducted as needed.
- Scans are performed by qualified personnel and organizational independence of the tester exists (not required to be a QSA or ASV).
controls.title: Internal Vulnerability Scans After a Significant Change

controls.body:
All access by application and system accounts and related access privileges are reviewed as follows:
- Periodically (at the frequency defined in the entity’s targeted risk analysis, which is performed according to all elements specified in Requirement 12.3.1).
- The application/system access remains appropriate for the function being performed.
- Any inappropriate access is addressed.
- Management acknowledges that access remains appropriate.
controls.title: Review Application and System Accounts

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall monitor for unauthorized access through a physical access point into a physical security perimeter.
controls.title: Monitoring Physical Access to Security Perimeter

controls.body: Inactive user accounts are removed or disabled within 90 days of inactivity.
controls.title: Disable Inactive User Accounts

controls.body: Information is encrypted or technical security measures are applied to protect the information in transit against unauthorized access.
controls.title: Encrypted Information During Transfer

controls.body: The access control system(s) is configured to enforce permissions assigned to individuals, applications, and systems based on job classification and function.
controls.title: Access Control System(s) Enforce Permissions

controls.body:
Electronic media with cardholder data is destroyed when no longer needed for business or legal reasons via one of the following:
- The electronic media is destroyed.
- The cardholder data is rendered unrecoverable so that it cannot be reconstructed.
controls.title: Media Destruction

controls.body: Read access to audit logs files is limited to those with a job-related need.
controls.title: Read Access to Logs

controls.body:
All security policies and operational procedures that are identified in Requirement 8 are:
- Documented.
- Kept up to date.
- In use.
- Known to all affected parties.
controls.title: Authentication Policies and Procedures

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall issue an alarm or alert in response to detected unauthorized access through a physical access point into a physical security perimeter to the personnel identified in the BES cyber security incident response plan within 15 minutes of detection.
controls.title: Physical Intrusion Alarms and Alerts to Security Perimeter

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall develop one or more documented information protection program(s) that includes method(s) for identification, protection and secure handling of BES cyber system information (BCSI).
controls.title: Information Protection Program

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall monitor each physical access control system for unauthorized physical access to a physical access control system.
controls.title: Monitoring Physical Access Control System

controls.body: Groups of information services, users and information systems shall be segregated in the organization’s networks.
controls.title: Segregation of Networks (27017)

controls.body:
Internal vulnerability scans are performed as follows:
- At least once every three months.
- High-risk and critical vulnerabilities (per the entity’s vulnerability risk rankings defined at Requirement 6.3.1) are resolved.
- Rescans are performed that confirm all high-risk and critical vulnerabilities (as noted above) have been resolved.
- Scan tool is kept up to date with latest vulnerability information.
- Scans are performed by qualified personnel and organizational independence of the tester exists.
controls.title: Quarterly Internal Vulnerability Scans

controls.body:
The following audit logs are reviewed at least once daily:
- All security events.
- Logs of all system components that store, process, or transmit CHD and/or SAD.
- Logs of all critical system components.
- Logs of all servers and system components that perform security functions (for example, network security controls, intrusion-detection systems/intrusion-prevention systems (IDS/IPS), authentication servers).
controls.title: Log Review

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall implement one or more information protection program(s) that includes method(s) to identify BES cyber system information (BCSI).
controls.title: Identification of BCSI

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall issue an alarm or alert in response to detected unauthorized physical access to a physical access control system to the personnel identified in the BES cyber security Incident response plan within 15 minutes of the detection.
controls.title: Physical Intrusion Alarms and Alerts to Access Control System
Cyber Security Plan

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall develop one or more documented process(es) for BES cyber asset reuse and disposal.
controls.title: BES Cyber Asset Reuse and Disposal Processes

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall log (through automated means or by personnel who control entry) entry of each individual with authorized unescorted physical access into each physical security perimeter, with information to identify the individual and date and time of entry.
controls.title: Logging Physical Access

controls.body:
External vulnerability scans are performed after any significant change as follows:
- Vulnerabilities that are scored 4.0 or higher by the CVSS are resolved.
- Rescans are conducted as needed.
- Scans are performed by qualified personnel and organizational independence of the tester exists (not required to be a QSA or ASV).
controls.title: External Vulnerability Scans After a Significant Change

controls.body: POI device surfaces are periodically inspected to detect tampering and unauthorized substitution.
controls.title: Periodic Inspection of Devices

controls.body: Exceptions and anomalies identified during the review process are addressed.
controls.title: Exceptions from Log Review

controls.body: The frequency of periodic POI device inspections and the type of inspections performed is defined in the entity’s targeted risk analysis, which is performed according to all elements specified in Requirement 12.3.1.
controls.title: Periodic Inspection of Devices

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall implement a process to evaluate criminal history records checks for authorizing access.
controls.title: Evaluation of Criminal History Check

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall retain physical access logs of entry of individuals with authorized unescorted physical access into each physical security perimeter for at least ninety calendar days.
controls.title: Retention of Physical Access Logs

controls.body:
Training is provided for personnel in POI environments to be aware of attempted tampering or replacement of POI devices, and includes:
- Verifying the identity of any third-party persons claiming to be repair or maintenance personnel, before granting them access to modify or troubleshoot devices.
- Procedures to ensure devices are not installed, replaced, or returned without verification.
- Being aware of suspicious behavior around devices.
- Reporting suspicious behavior and indications of device tampering or substitution to appropriate personnel.
controls.title: Personnel Training on Device Protection

controls.body:
All security policies and operational procedures that are identified in Requirement 10 are:
- Documented.
- Kept up to date.
- In use.
- Known to all affected parties.
controls.title: Logging and Monitoring Policies and Procedures

controls.body: Retain audit log history for at least 12 months, with at least the most recent three months immediately available for analysis.
controls.title: Audit Log Retention

controls.body:
Systems are configured to the correct and consistent time as follows:
- One or more designated time servers are in use.
- Only the designated central time server(s) receives time from external sources.
- Time received from external sources is based on International Atomic Time or Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
- The designated time server(s) accept time updates only from specific industry-accepted external sources.
- Where there is more than one designated time server, the time servers peer with one another to keep accurate time.
- Internal systems receive time information only from designated central time server(s).
controls.title: Time Settings and Synchronization

controls.body: Audit logs capture all access to audit logs.
controls.title: Access Restriction to Audit Log

controls.body:
Each responsible entity shall restrict physical access to cabling and other non-programmable communication components used for connection between applicable cyber assets within the same electronic security perimeter in those instances when such cabling and components are located outside of a physical security perimeter. Where physical access restrictions to such cabling and components are not implemented, the responsible entity shall implement one or more of the following:
* encryption of data that transit such cabling and components; or
* monitoring the status of the communication link composed of such cabling and components and issuing an alarm or alert in response to detected communication failures to the personnel identified in the BES cyber security incident response plan within 15 minutes of detection; or
* an equally effective logical protection.
controls.title: Restricting Physical Access

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall verify at least once every 15 calendar months that access to the designated storage locations for BES cyber system information, whether physical or electronic, are correct and are those that the responsible entity determines are necessary for performing assigned work functions.
controls.title: Verification of Access to Storage Locations

controls.body: Prior to the disposal of applicable cyber assets that contain BES cyber system information, the responsible entity shall take action to prevent the unauthorized retrieval of BES cyber system information from the cyber asset or destroy the data storage media.
controls.title: BES Cyber System Information Disposal and Destruction

controls.body: Audit logs are enabled and active for all system components and cardholder data.
controls.title: Audit Log Implementation

controls.body: Audit logs capture all individual user access to cardholder data.
controls.title: User Access Logs

controls.body:
Each responsible entity shall, where technically feasible, either:
* limit the number of unsuccessful authentication attempts; or
* generate alerts after a threshold of unsuccessful authentication attempts.
controls.title: Authentication Attempts

controls.body: Audit logs capture all invalid logical access attempts.
controls.title: Audit Logs for Invalid Login Attempts

controls.body:
Audit logs capture the following:
- All initialization of new audit logs, and
- All starting, stopping, or pausing of the existing audit logs.
controls.title: Logs for Initialization, Stopping or Pausing of Audit Logs

controls.body:
A change-and tamper-detection mechanism is deployed as follows:
- To alert personnel to unauthorized modification (including indicators of compromise, changes, additions, and deletions) to the HTTP headers and the contents of payment pages as received by the consumer browser.
- The mechanism is configured to evaluate the received HTTP header and payment page.
- The mechanism functions are performed as follows:
    * At least once every seven days
OR
    * Periodically (at the frequency defined in the entity’s targeted risk analysis, which is performed according to all elements specified in Requirement 12.3.1).
controls.title: Change-and-Tamper-Detection Mechanism

controls.body:
Audit logs record the following details for each auditable event:
- User identification.
- Type of event.
- Date and time.
- Success and failure indication.
- Origination of event.
- Identity or name of affected data, system component, resource, or service (for example, name and protocol).
controls.title: Audit Log Entries

controls.body: Logs that record activities, exceptions, faults and other relevant events shall be produced, stored, protected and analyzed.
controls.title: Logging (27017)

controls.body: There shall be online information available to the data subjects about the smart city deployment strategy, the purpose(s) and measures set in place to protect personal data.
controls.title: Online Information on IoT Data Processing

controls.body:
Additional requirement for service providers only: Failures of critical security control systems are detected, alerted, and addressed promptly, including but not limited to failure of the following critical security control systems:
- Network security controls.
- IDS/IPS.
- FIM.
- Anti-malware solutions.
- Physical access controls.
- Logical access controls.
- Audit logging mechanisms.
- Segmentation controls (if used).
controls.title: Timely Detection and Reporting for Service Providers

controls.body: File integrity monitoring or change-detection mechanisms is used on audit logs to ensure that existing log data cannot be changed without generating alerts.
controls.title: File Integrity Monitoring

controls.body: Automated mechanisms are used to perform audit log reviews.
controls.title: Automated Log Review

controls.body: Logs of all other system components (those not specified in Requirement 10.4.1) are reviewed periodically.
controls.title: Other System Components Log Review

controls.body: The frequency of periodic log reviews for all other system components (not defined in Requirement 10.4.1) is defined in the entity’s targeted risk analysis, which is performed according to all elements specified in Requirement 12.3.1.
controls.title: Risk-Based Log Review

controls.body: The privacy policy and DPO contact details shall be accessible in no more than three clicks from the Applicant's website home page.
controls.title: Website Information Ease of Access

controls.body:
Failures of critical security control systems are detected, alerted, and addressed promptly, including but not limited to failure of the following critical security control systems:
- Network security controls.
- IDS/IPS.
- Change-detection mechanisms.
- Anti-malware solutions.
- Physical access controls.
- Logical access controls.
- Audit logging mechanisms.
- Segmentation controls (if used).
- Audit log review mechanisms.
- Automated security testing tools (if used).
controls.title: Timely Detection and Reporting

controls.body:
Additional requirement for service providers only: TPSPs support their customers’ requests for information to meet Requirements
12.8.4 and 12.8.5 by providing the following upon customer request:
- PCI DSS compliance status information for any service the TPSP performs on behalf of customers (Requirement 12.8.4).
- Information about which PCI DSS requirements are the responsibility of the TPSP and which are the responsibility of the customer, including any shared responsibilities (Requirement 12.8.5).""12.9.2 Additional requirement for service providers only: TPSPs support their customers’ requests for information to meet Requirements
12.8.4 and 12.8.5 by providing the following upon customer request:
- PCI DSS compliance status information for any service the TPSP performs on behalf of customers (Requirement 12.8.4).
- Information about which PCI DSS requirements are the responsibility of the TPSP and which are the responsibility of the customer, including any shared responsibilities (Requirement 12.8.5).
controls.title: TPSP Support for Customers' PCI DSS Compliance

controls.body: The frequency of periodic training for incident response personnel is defined in the entity’s targeted risk analysis, which is performed according to all elements specified in Requirement 12.3.1.
controls.title: Risk Analysis for Frequency of Incident Response Training

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall develop a documented one or more documented visitor control program(s).
controls.title: Documented Visitor Control Program

controls.body:
All security policies and operational procedures that are identified in Requirement 11 are:
- Documented.
- Kept up to date.
- In use.
- Known to all affected parties.
controls.title: Vulnerability and Penetration Testing Policies and Procedures

controls.body:
The security incident response plan includes monitoring and responding to alerts from security monitoring systems, including but not limited to:
- Intrusion-detection and intrusion-prevention systems.
- Network security controls.
- Change-detection mechanisms for critical files.
- The change-and tamper-detection mechanism for payment pages.
- Detection of unauthorized wireless access points.
controls.title: Incident Response to Alerts from Security Monitoring System

controls.body:
Audit log capability is enabled for each customer’s environment that is consistent with PCI DSS Requirement 10, including:
- Logs are enabled for common third-party applications.
- Logs are active by default.
- Logs are available for review only by the owning customer.
- Log locations are clearly communicated to the owning customer.
- Log data and availability is consistent with PCI DSS Requirement 10.
controls.title: Audit Log Enabled for Each Customer's Cardholder Data Environment

controls.body: Where POS POI terminals at the merchant or payment acceptance location use SSL and/or early TLS, the entity confirms the devices are not susceptible to any known exploits for those protocols.
controls.title: POS POI Terminal SSL/TLS Requirement

controls.body: The organization’s approach to managing information security and its implementation including people,  processes and technologies shall be reviewed independently at planned intervals, or when significant changes occur.
controls.title: Independent Review of Information Security (27018)

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall develop one or more documented process(es) for the reuse and disposal of cyber assets that contain BES cyber system information (BCSI).
controls.title: BES Cyber Asset Reuse and Disposal Processes

controls.body:
Authorized and unauthorized wireless access points are managed as follows:
- The presence of wireless (Wi-Fi) access points is tested for,
- All authorized and unauthorized wireless access points are detected and identified,
- Testing, detection, and identification occurs at least once every three months.
- If automated monitoring is used, personnel are notified via generated alerts.
controls.title: Management of Wireless Access Points

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall require continuous escorted access of visitors (individuals who are provided access but are not authorized for unescorted physical access) within each physical security perimeter, except during CIP exceptional circumstances.
controls.title: Visitor Access

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall require manual or automated logging of visitor entry into and exit from the physical security perimeter that includes the date and time of the initial entry and last exit, the visitor’s name, and the name of an individual point of contact responsible for the visitor, except during CIP exceptional circumstances.
controls.title: Visitor Log

controls.body: Information and other supporting assets associated with information and information processing facilities are identified and an inventory of these assets is drawn up and maintained.
controls.title: Inventory of Assets

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall perform maintenance and testing of each physical access control system and locally mounted hardware or devices at the physical security perimeter at least once every 24 calendar months to ensure they function properly.
controls.title: Physical Access Control System Testing and Maintenance

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall retain visitor logs for at least ninety calendar days.
controls.title: Retain Visitor Log

controls.body: Prior to the disposal of applicable cyber assets that contain BES cyber system information (BCSI), the responsible entity shall take action to prevent the unauthorized retrieval of BCSI from the cyber asset or destroy the data storage media.
controls.title: BCSI Disposal and Destruction

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall develop a documented one or more documented physical access control system program(s).
controls.title: Documented Physical Access System Testing and Maintenance Program

controls.body: The effectiveness of logical separation controls used to separate customer environments is confirmed at least once every six months via penetration testing.
controls.title: Effectiveness of Logical Separation Controls

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall develop and implement a documented process for enabling ports and services.
controls.title: Documented Process for Enabling Ports and Services

controls.body: A cloud service customer's virtual environment running on a cloud service shall be protected from other cloud service customers and unauthorized persons.
controls.title: Segregation in Virtual Computing Environments

controls.body: Virtual machines in a cloud computing environment shall be hardened to meet business needs.
controls.title: Virtual Machine Hardening

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall protect against the use of unnecessary physical input/output ports used for network connectivity, console commands or removable media.
controls.title: Physical Input/Output Ports

controls.body: The organization defines and implements procedures to prevent the unauthorized creation or transmission of images of vehicles, components or parts classified as requiring protection.
controls.title: Image Material Protection

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall implement a patch management process for tracking, evaluating, and installing cyber security patches for applicable cyber assets. The tracking portion shall include the identification of a source or sources that the responsible entity tracks for the release of cyber security patches for applicable cyber assets that are updateable and for which a patching source exists.
controls.title: Patch Management Process

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall at least once every 35 calendar days, evaluate security patches for applicability that have been released since the last evaluation from the source or sources identified in requirement CIP-007.R2-2.1 - Patch Management Process.
controls.title: Periodic Evaluation of Security Patches

controls.body: For each mitigation plan created or revised in the requirement "CIP-007.R2-2.3 Security Patch Management", each responsible entity shall implement the plan within the timeframe specified in the plan, unless a revision to the plan or an extension to the timeframe specified in requirement "CIP-007.R2-2.3 Security Patch Management" is approved by the CIP senior manager or delegate.
controls.title: Implementation of Dated Mitigation Plan

controls.body: A project management methodology developed and implemented emphasizing, including but not limited to, the security classification process and resulting security measures.
controls.title: Project Security Classifications
Access Authentication to the Camera

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall develop and implement a documented process for the prevention of malicious code.
controls.title: Documented Malicious Code Prevention Process

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall deploy method(s) to deter, detect or prevent malicious code.
controls.title: Malicious Code Identification and Prevention

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall mitigate the threat of detected malicious code.
controls.title: Malicious Code Identification Mitigation

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall have a process for the update of the signatures or patterns for those methods identified in the requirement "CIP-007.R3-3.1- Malicious Code Identification and Prevention" that use signatures or patterns. The process must address testing and installing the signatures or patterns.
controls.title: Malicious Code Prevention
Access Restriction to the Video Server

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall develop and implement a documented process for log monitoring and management.
controls.title: Documented Log Management Process

controls.body:
Internal vulnerability scans are performed via authenticated scanning as follows:
- Systems that are unable to accept credentials for authenticated scanning are documented.
- Sufficient privileges are used for those systems that accept credentials for scanning.
- If accounts used for authenticated scanning can be used for interactive login, they are managed in accordance with Requirement 8.2.2.
controls.title: Authenticated Vulnerability Scans
Log Configuration

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall where technically feasible, retain applicable event logs identified in "CIP-007.R4-4.1 - Log Configuration" for at least the last 90 consecutive calendar days except under CIP exceptional circumstances.
controls.title: Log Retention

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall review a summarization or sampling of logged events as determined by the responsible entity at intervals no greater than 15 calendar days to identify undetected cyber security incidents.
controls.title: Log Review

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall develop and implement a documented authentication and authorization process for system access.
controls.title: Documented Authentication and Authorization Process

controls.body: The organization has adopted a classification scheme to classify information assets based on the protection goals of information security (confidentiality, integrity and availability) and serve as a basis for the handling of supporting assets.
controls.title: Classification and Handling of Information Assets

controls.body:
External vulnerability scans are performed as follows:
- At least once every three months.
- By a PCI SSC Approved Scanning Vendor (ASV).
- Vulnerabilities are resolved and ASV Program Guide requirements for a passing scan are met.
- Rescans are performed as needed to confirm that vulnerabilities are resolved per the ASV Program Guide requirements for a passing scan.
controls.title: Quarterly External Vulnerability Scans

controls.body: A set of policies for information security are defined, approved by management, published and communicated to employees and relevant external business partners. These policies are reviewed at planned intervals or if significant changes occur.
controls.title: Policies for Information Security

controls.body:
A change-detection mechanism (for example, file integrity monitoring tools) is deployed as follows:
- To alert personnel to unauthorized modification (including changes, additions, and deletions) of critical files.
- To perform critical file comparisons at least once weekly.
controls.title: Change Detection Mechanism

controls.body: Appropriate request documentation and authorization process are in place for individuals requiring access to security areas where vehicles, components or parts classified as requiring protection are manufactured, processed or stored.
controls.title: Access to Security Areas

controls.body:
An overall information security policy is:
- Established.
- Published.
- Maintained.
- Disseminated to all relevant personnel, as well as to relevant vendors and business partners.
controls.title: Card Data Security Policy

controls.body: Vulnerability assessments are performed on a quarterly basis to identify threats and vulnerabilities in IT systems. Issues are identified, analyzed and addressed in a timely manner.
controls.title: Vulnerability Assessment and Remediation

controls.body: A) The Data Protection Officer (DPO) or a legal expert with adequate expertise shall have checked and validated that the video camera deployment does not infringe the applicable laws and regulations for video surveillance, including the applicable national regulations.
controls.title: Camera Deployment Validation by the DPO
Information on Video Surveillance

controls.body: Rules for the secure development of software and systems shall be established and applied.
controls.title: Secure Development Life Cycle (27017)

controls.body: The organization acquires, develops and manages IT systems in accordance with its software development policy that includes information security considerations.
controls.title: Information Security of IT Systems

controls.body:
The information security policy is:
- Reviewed at least once every 12 months.
- Updated as needed to reflect changes to business objectives or risks to the environment.
controls.title: Review of Card Data Security Policy

controls.body: The organization monitors for intrusion on its premises where vehicles, components, or classified parts that require protection are manufactured, processed, or stored. Alarm mechanisms have been installed to detect intrusions in real-time.
controls.title: Secure Intrusion Monitoring
Video Network Protection

controls.body: The organization has developed and implemented a process for protecting vehicles, components, and parts against unauthorized viewing, image recording, and access during transport.
controls.title: Transport of Vehicles, Components and Parts

controls.body: The security policy clearly defines information security roles and responsibilities for all personnel, and all personnel are aware of and acknowledge their information security responsibilities.
controls.title: Information Security Roles and Responsibilities

controls.body: The organization implements appropriate technical and organizational measures for the security and protection of personal information and for processing personal information in line with data subject rights.
controls.title: Technical and Organizational Measures

controls.body: The organization has appointed a Data Protection Officer (DPO), where legally required, or a person responsible for the development and implementation of data protection policies and procedures.
controls.title: Data Protection Officer

controls.body: Procedures for administrative operations of a cloud computing environment shall be defined, documented and monitored.
controls.title: Administrator's Operational Security

controls.body: Responsibility for information security is formally assigned to a Chief Information Security Officer or other information security knowledgeable member of executive management.
controls.title: Information Security Role in Executive Management

controls.body:
Each PCI DSS requirement that provides flexibility for how frequently it is performed (for example, requirements to be performed periodically) is supported by a targeted risk analysis that is documented and includes:
- Identification of the assets being protected.
- Identification of the threat(s) that the requirement is protecting against.
- Identification of factors that contribute to the likelihood and/or impact of a threat being realized.
- Resulting analysis that determines, and includes justification for, how frequently the requirement must be performed to minimize the likelihood of the threat being realized.
- Review of each targeted risk analysis at least once every 12 months to determine whether the results are still valid or if an updated risk analysis is needed.
- Performance of updated risk analyses when needed, as determined by the annual review.
controls.title: Risk Analysis of Flexible Periodic Requirements

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall identify individuals who have authorized access to shared accounts.
controls.title: Shared Accounts

controls.body: All information security responsibilities within the organization are clearly defined, documented, assigned and communicated.
controls.title: Information Security Roles and Responsibilities

controls.body: A policy and supporting security measures are implemented to protect information accessed, processed or stored at teleworking sites.
controls.title: Teleworking

controls.body:
A targeted risk analysis is performed for each PCI DSS requirement that the entity meets with the customized approach, to include:
- Documented evidence detailing each element specified in Appendix D: Customized Approach (including, at a minimum, a controls matrix and risk analysis).
- Approval of documented evidence by senior management.
- Performance of the targeted analysis of risk at least once every 12 months.
controls.title: Risk Analysis for Customized Approach

controls.body: The organization has defined and implemented security zones along with the associated protective measures to provide physical protection to areas that contain sensitive information assets.
controls.title: Physical Security Zones

controls.body:
Cryptographic cipher suites and protocols in use are documented and reviewed at least once every 12 months, including at least the following:
- An up-to-date inventory of all cryptographic cipher suites and protocols in use, including purpose and where used.
- Active monitoring of industry trends regarding continued viability of all cryptographic cipher suites and protocols in use.
- A documented strategy to respond to anticipated changes in cryptographic vulnerabilities.
controls.title: Cryptographic Cipher Suites and Protocols

controls.body: The organization has implemented appropriate measures to protect information transmitted over public or private networks from unauthorized access.
controls.title: Information Protection During Transfer

controls.body: A policy and supporting security measures are adopted to manage the risks introduced by using mobile IT devices and mobile data storage devices.
controls.title: Management of Mobile IT and Data Storage Devices

controls.body:
Hardware and software technologies in use are reviewed at least once every 12 months, including at least the following:
- Analysis that the technologies continue to receive security fixes from vendors promptly.
- Analysis that the technologies continue to support (and do not preclude) the entity’s PCI DSS compliance.
- Documentation of any industry announcements or trends related to a technology, such as when a vendor has announced “end of life” plans for a technology.
- Documentation of a plan, approved by senior management, to remediate outdated technologies, including those for which vendors have announced “end of life” plans.
controls.title: Review of Hardware and Software Technologies

controls.body:
Additional requirement for service providers only: Responsibility is established by executive management for the protection of cardholder data and a PCI DSS compliance program to include:
- Overall accountability for maintaining PCI DSS compliance.
- Defining a charter for a PCI DSS compliance program and communication to executive management.
controls.title: Executive Management Assignment of PCI DSS Compliance Responsibility

controls.body:
Additional requirement for service providers only: Reviews are performed at least once every three months to confirm that personnel are performing their tasks in accordance with all security policies and operational procedures. Reviews are performed by personnel other than those responsible for performing the given task and include, but are not limited to, the following tasks:
- Daily log reviews.
- Configuration reviews for network security controls.
- Applying configuration standards to new systems.
- Responding to security alerts.
- Change-management processes.
controls.title: Security Policy Compliance Quarterly Reviews

controls.body:
Additional requirement for service providers only: Reviews conducted in accordance with Requirement 12.4.2 are documented to include:
- Results of the reviews.
- Documented remediation actions taken for any tasks that were found to not be performed at Requirement 12.4.2.
- Review and sign-off of results by personnel assigned responsibility for the PCI DSS compliance program.
controls.title: Security Compliance Reviews for Service Providers

controls.body: An inventory of system components that are in scope for PCI DSS, including a description of function/use, is maintained and kept current.
controls.title: Asset Inventory in PCI DSS Scope

controls.body: Additional requirement for service providers only: Significant changes to organizational structure result in a documented (internal) review of the impact to PCI DSS scope and applicability of controls, with results communicated to executive management.
controls.title: Review of PCI DSS Scope Following Significant Change

controls.body: A formal security awareness program is implemented to make all personnel aware of the entity’s information security policy and procedures, and their role in protecting the cardholder data.
controls.title: Security Awareness Program

controls.body:
The security awareness program is:
- Reviewed at least once every 12 months, and
- Updated as needed to address any new threats and vulnerabilities that may impact the security of the entity’s CDE, or the information provided to personnel about their role in protecting cardholder data.
controls.title: Review of Security Awareness Program

controls.body:
Personnel receive security awareness training as follows:
- Upon hire and at least once every 12 months.
- Multiple methods of communication are used.
- Personnel acknowledge at least once every 12 months that they have read and understood the information security policy and procedures.
controls.title: Annual Security Awareness Training

controls.body: Potential personnel who will have access to the CDE are screened, within the constraints of local laws, prior to hire to minimize the risk of attacks from internal sources.
controls.title: Screening of Potential Personnel

controls.body: An established process is implemented for engaging TPSPs, including proper due diligence prior to engagement.
controls.title: TPSP Engagement Process

controls.body: Additional requirement for service providers only: TPSPs acknowledge in writing to customers that they are responsible for the security of account data the TPSP possesses or otherwise stores, processes, or transmits on behalf of the customer, or to the extent that they could impact the security of the customer’s CDE.
controls.title: Acknowledged Card Security Responsibilities by TPSPs

controls.body:
At least once every 12 months, the security incident response plan is:
- Reviewed and the content is updated as needed.
- Tested, including all elements listed in Requirement 12.10.1.
controls.title: Review and Test of the Incident Response Plan

controls.body: Affirmative consent is obtained and maintained from individuals prior to any processing of their sensitive personal information. Individuals are provided with a mechanism to withdraw their consent, and any such requests are documented and retained in accordance with organization policies.
controls.title: Consent on Processing of Sensitive Personal Information

controls.body: Specific personnel are designated to be available on a 24/7 basis to respond to suspected or confirmed security incidents.
controls.title: Incident Response Team

controls.body: A) The Data Processing Impact Assessment shall have evaluated the risk for the data subjects that the data processing of the vehicle communicates criminal offenses or other infractions.
controls.title: Data Processing Revealing Criminal Offenses or Other Infractions

controls.body:
Incident response procedures are in place, to be initiated upon the detection of stored PAN anywhere it is not expected, and include:
- Determining what to do if PAN is discovered outside the CDE, including its retrieval, secure deletion, and/or migration into the currently defined CDE, as applicable.
- Identifying whether sensitive authentication data is stored with PAN.
- Determining where the account data came from and how it ended up where it was not expected.
- Remediating data leaks or process gaps that resulted in the account data being where it was not expected.
controls.title: Incident Response to PAN in Unexpected Locations

controls.body:
Logical separation is implemented as follows:
- The provider cannot access its customers’ environments without authorization.
- Customers cannot access the provider’s environment without authorization.
controls.title: Logical Separation of Customers' Environments

controls.body: Controls are implemented such that each customer can only access resources allocated to them.
controls.title: Access Restriction to Resources

controls.body:
Each responsible entity shall no later than 60 calendar days after a change to the roles or responsibilities, cyber security incident response groups or individuals, or technology that the responsible entity determines would impact the ability to execute the plan:
3.2.1. Update the cyber security incident response plan(s); and
3.2.2. Notify each person or group with a defined role in the cyber security incident response plan of the updates.
controls.title: Changes to Roles and Responsibilities

controls.body: Required privileges are approved by authorized personnel.
controls.title: Documented Access Approval

controls.body: Roles and responsibilities for performing activities in Requirement 8 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.title: Roles and Responsibilities

controls.body: Processes or mechanisms are implemented to support and/or facilitate prompt forensic investigations in the event of a suspected or confirmed security incident for any customer.
controls.title: Forensic Investigation Process

controls.body:
Processes or mechanisms are implemented for reporting and addressing suspected or confirmed security incidents and vulnerabilities, including:
- Customers can securely report security incidents and vulnerabilities to the provider.
- The provider addresses and remediates suspected or confirmed security incidents and vulnerabilities according to Requirement 6.3.1.
controls.title: Reporting and Addressing Security Incidents and Vulnerabilities

controls.body:
Accounts used by third parties to access, support, or maintain system components via remote access are managed as follows:
- Enabled only during the time period needed and disabled when not in use.
- Use is monitored for unexpected activity.
controls.title: Third Party Access IDs

controls.body:
Responsibility is established by executive management for the protection of account data and a PCI DSS compliance program that includes:
- Overall accountability for maintaining PCI DSS compliance.
- Defining a charter for a PCI DSS compliance program.
- Providing updates to executive management and board of directors on PCI DSS compliance initiatives and issues, including remediation activities, at least once every 12 months.

PCI DSS Reference: Requirement 12
controls.title: Executive Management Established Responsibility

controls.body:
Invalid authentication attempts are limited by:
- Locking out the user ID after not more than 10 attempts.
- Setting the lockout duration to a minimum of 30 minutes or until the user’s identity is confirmed.
controls.title: Invalid Authentication

controls.body: All users are assigned a unique ID before access to system components or cardholder data is allowed.
controls.title: Assignment of Unique ID

controls.body: Additional requirement for service providers only: Service providers with remote access to customer premises use unique authentication factors for each customer premises.
controls.title: Service Providers with Remote Access

controls.body:
Addition, deletion, and modification of user IDs, authentication factors, and other identifier objects are managed as follows:
- Authorized with the appropriate approval.
- Implemented with only the privileges specified on the documented approval.
controls.title: User Provisioning and De-provisioning

controls.body:
Additional requirement for service providers only: All service providers with existing connection points to POS POI terminals that use SSL and/or early TLS as defined in A2.1 have a formal Risk Mitigation and Migration Plan in place that includes:
- Description of usage, including what data is being transmitted, types and number of systems that use and/or support SSL/early TLS, and type of environment.
- Risk-assessment results and risk-reduction controls in place.
- Description of processes to monitor for new vulnerabilities associated with SSL/early TLS.
- Description of change control processes that are implemented to ensure SSL/early TLS is not implemented into new environments.
- Overview of migration project plan to replace SSL/early TLS at a future date.
controls.title: Risk Mitigation Plan for Using SSL and/or Early TLS

controls.body:
Security vulnerabilities are identified and managed as follows:
- New security vulnerabilities are identified using industry-recognized sources for security vulnerability information, including alerts from international and national computer emergency response teams (CERTs).
- Vulnerabilities are assigned a risk ranking based on industry best practices and consideration of potential impact.
- Risk rankings identify, at a minimum, all vulnerabilities considered to be high-risk or critical to the environment.
- Vulnerabilities for bespoke and custom, and third-party software (for example operating systems and databases) are covered.
controls.title: Security Vulnerability Management

controls.body: Access for terminated users is immediately revoked.
controls.title: Revoke Access of Terminated Users

controls.body: Additional requirement for service providers only: All service providers provide a secure service offering.
controls.title: Secure Service Offering

controls.body: Strong cryptography is used to render all authentication factors unreadable during transmission and storage on all system components.
controls.title: Strong Cryptography for Authentication Credentials
IoT Firmware Updates

controls.body: User identity is verified before modifying any authentication factor.
controls.title: Modification of Authentication Credentials

controls.body:
A formal PCI DSS compliance program is in place that includes:
- Definition of activities for maintaining and monitoring overall PCI DSS compliance, including business-as-usual activities.
- Annual PCI DSS assessment processes.
- Processes for the continuous validation of PCI DSS requirements (for example, daily, weekly, every three months, as applicable per the requirement).
- A process for performing business-impact analysis to determine potential PCI DSS impacts for strategic business decisions.

PCI DSS Reference: Requirements 1-12
controls.title: Formal PCI DSS Compliance Program

controls.body:
If passwords/passphrases are used as authentication factors to meet Requirement 8.3.1, they are set and reset for each user as follows:
- Set to a unique value for first-time use and upon reset.
- Forced to be changed immediately after the first use.
controls.title: First Time Passwords

controls.body: Individuals are not allowed to submit a new password/passphrase that is the same as any of the last four passwords/passphrases used.
controls.title: Password History

controls.body: MFA is implemented for all access into the CDE.
controls.title: Multi-Factor Authentication

controls.body:
Authentication policies and procedures are documented and communicated to all users including:
- Guidance on selecting strong authentication factors.
- Guidance for how users should protect their authentication factors.
- Instructions not to reuse previously used passwords/passphrases.
- Instructions to change passwords/passphrases if there is any suspicion or knowledge that the password/passphrases have been compromised and how to report the incident.
controls.title: User Authentication Guidance

controls.body:
Additional requirement for service providers only: If passwords/passphrases are used as the only authentication factor for customer user access to cardholder data (i.e., in any single- factor authentication implementation), then guidance is provided to customer users including:
- Guidance for customers to change their user passwords/passphrases periodically.
- Guidance as to when, and under what circumstances, passwords/passphrases are to be changed.
controls.title: Service Provider Authentication

controls.body:
PCI DSS compliance roles and responsibilities are specifically defined and formally assigned to one or more personnel, including:
- Managing PCI DSS business-as-usual activities.
- Managing annual PCI DSS assessments.
- Managing continuous validation of PCI DSS requirements (for example, daily, weekly, every three months, as applicable per the requirement).
- Managing business-impact analysis to determine potential PCI DSS impacts for strategic business decisions.

PCI DSS Reference: Requirement 12
controls.title: PCI DSS Compliance Roles and Responsibilities

controls.body: MFA is implemented for all non-console access into the CDE for personnel with administrative access.
controls.title: Multi-Factor Authentication for Non-console Access

controls.body:
If segmentation is used to isolate the CDE from other networks, penetration tests are performed on segmentation controls as follows:
- At least once every 12 months and after any changes to segmentation controls/methods
- Covering all segmentation controls/methods in use.
- According to the entity’s defined penetration testing methodology.
- Confirming that the segmentation controls/methods are operational and effective, and isolate the CDE from all out-of-scope systems.
- Confirming effectiveness of any use of isolation to separate systems with differing security levels (see Requirement 2.2.3).
- Performed by a qualified internal resource or qualified external third party.
- Organizational independence of the tester exists (not required to be a QSA or ASV).
controls.title: Penetration Test on Isolated CDE

controls.body:
MFA systems are implemented as follows:
- The MFA system is not susceptible to replay attacks.
- MFA systems cannot be bypassed by any users, including administrative users unless specifically documented, and authorized by management on an exception basis, for a limited time period.
- At least two different types of authentication factors are used.
- Success of all authentication factors is required before access is granted.
controls.title: Multi-Factor Authentication Configuration

controls.body: Passwords/passphrases for any application and system accounts that can be used for interactive login are not hard coded in scripts, configuration/property files, or bespoke and custom source code.
controls.title: Passwords for Interactive Login System Accounts

controls.body:
Up-to-date PCI DSS and/or information security training is provided at least once every 12 months to personnel with PCI DSS compliance responsibilities (as identified in A3.1.3).

PCI DSS Reference: Requirement 12
controls.title: Up-to-date Information Security Training

controls.body:
PCI DSS scope impact for all changes to systems or networks is determined, including additions of new systems and new network connections. Processes include:
- Performing a formal PCI DSS impact assessment.
- Identifying applicable PCI DSS requirements to the system or network.
- Updating PCI DSS scope as appropriate.
- Documented sign-off of the results of the impact assessment by responsible personnel (as defined in A3.1.3).

PCI DSS Reference: Scope of PCI DSS Requirements; Requirements 1-12
controls.title: Impact of PCI DSS Scope Changes
Resilience to Outage

controls.body:
Upon completion of a change, all relevant PCI DSS requirements are confirmed to be implemented on all new or changed systems and networks, and documentation is updated as applicable.

PCI DSS Reference: Scope of PCI DSS Requirements; Requirement 1-12
controls.title: Verification of PCI DSS Requirements after a Change

controls.body: A) The transmission of personal data by IoT devices shall be encrypted.
controls.title: IoT Encryption

controls.body:
A data-discovery methodology is implemented that:
- Confirms PCI DSS scope.
- Locates all sources and locations of cleartext PAN at least once every three months and upon significant changes to the CDE or processes.
- Addresses the potential for cleartext PAN to reside on systems and networks outside the currently defined CDE.

PCI DSS Reference: Scope of PCI DSS Requirements
controls.title: Data Discovery Techniques

controls.body:
Data discovery methods are confirmed as follows:
- Effectiveness of methods is tested.
- Methods are able to discover cleartext PAN on all types of system components and file formats in use.
- The effectiveness of data-discovery methods is confirmed at least once every 12 months.

PCI DSS Reference: Scope of PCI DSS Requirements
controls.title: Effectiveness of Data Discovery Techniques

controls.body:
Hardware and software technologies are reviewed at least once every 12 months to confirm whether they continue to meet the organization’s PCI DSS requirements.

PCI DSS Reference: Requirements 2, 6, 12.
controls.title: Annual Software and Hardware Review

controls.body: Review cloud service providers used by the organization which do not allow multi-factor authentication.
controls.title: Cloud Services Without MFA

controls.body: Authenticate all local and remote users before granting access to organizational systems and data.
controls.title: User Authentication

controls.body:
Response procedures are implemented to be initiated upon the detection of cleartext PAN outside the CDE to include:
    Determining what to do if cleartext PAN is discovered outside the CDE, including its retrieval, secure deletion, and/or migration into the currently defined CDE, as applicable.
- Determining how the data ended up outside the CDE.
- Remediating data leaks or process gaps that resulted in the data being outside the CDE.
- Identifying the source of the data.
- Identifying whether any track data is stored with the PANs.
controls.title: Response Procedures Initiated upon Detection of Clear-text PAN

controls.body:
A methodology is implemented for the prompt identification of attack patterns and undesirable behavior across systems that includes:
- Identification of anomalies or suspicious activity as it occurs.
- Issuance of prompt alerts upon detection of suspicious activity or anomaly to responsible personnel.
- Response to alerts in accordance with documented response procedures.

PCI DSS Reference: Requirements 10, 12
controls.title: Techniques for Identifying Patterns of Attack and Undesirable Actions

controls.body:
Mechanisms are implemented for detecting and preventing cleartext PAN from leaving the CDE via an unauthorized channel, method, or process, including mechanisms that are:
- Actively running.
- Configured to detect and prevent cleartext PAN leaving the CDE via an unauthorized channel, method, or process.
- Generating audit logs and alerts upon detection of cleartext PAN leaving the CDE via an unauthorized channel, method, or process.

PCI DSS Reference: Scope of PCI DSS Requirements, Requirement 12
controls.title: Techniques for Detection of Clear-text PAN

controls.body: A) There shall be a restrictive access policy to the IoT network and data that conforms to the "least privilege" access principle.
controls.title: Least Privileged Principle

controls.body: Roles and responsibilities for performing activities in Requirement 5 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.title: Roles and Responsibilities

controls.body:
All user access to system components for users and administrators is authenticated via at least one of the following authentication factors:
- Something you know, such as a password or passphrase.
- Something you have, such as a token device or smart card.
- Something you are, such as a biometric element.
controls.title: Authentication

controls.body:
MFA is implemented for all remote network access originating from outside the entity’s network that could access or impact the CDE as follows:
- All remote access by all personnel, both users and administrators, originating from outside the entity’s network.
- All remote access by third parties and vendors.
controls.title: Multi-Factor Authentication for Remote Access

controls.body:
If passwords/passphrases are used as authentication factors to meet Requirement 8.3.1, they meet the following minimum level of complexity:
- A minimum length of 12 characters (or IF the system does not support 12 characters, a minimum length of eight characters).
- Contain both numeric and alphabetic characters.
controls.title: Password Requirement

controls.body: A) The IoT devices shall be deployed in a manner that minimises the risk of theft.
controls.title: Physical Protection

controls.body:
A visitor log is used to maintain a physical record of visitor activity within the facility and within sensitive areas, including:
- The visitor’s name and the organization represented.
- The date and time of the visit.
- The name of the personnel authorizing physical access.
- Retaining the log for at least three months, unless otherwise restricted by law.
controls.title: Visitor Log

controls.body: Roles and responsibilities for performing activities in Requirement 10 are documented, assigned, and understood.
controls.title: Roles and Responsibilities

controls.body:
Procedures are implemented for authorizing and managing physical access of personnel to the CDE, including:
- Identifying personnel.
- Managing changes to an individual’s physical access requirements.
- Revoking or terminating personnel identification.
- Limiting access to the identification process or system to authorized personnel.
controls.title: Physical Access Control

controls.body:
Exploitable vulnerabilities and security weaknesses found during penetration testing are corrected as follows:
- In accordance with the entity’s assessment of the risk posed by the security issue as defined in Requirement 6.3.1.
- Penetration testing is repeated to verify the corrections.
controls.title: Correction of Vulnerabilities and Retesting

controls.body: Enable software firewalls on all of the computers, laptops and servers managed by the organization.
controls.title: Software Firewall

controls.body: Additional requirement for multi-tenant service providers only: Multi-tenant service providers support their customers for external penetration testing per Requirements 11.4.3 and 11.4.4.
controls.title: Customer Support for External Penetration Testing

controls.body: Development, testing and operational/production environments are segregated for changes to the information systems.
controls.title: Segregation of Environments

controls.body:
Additional requirement for service providers only: If segmentation is used to isolate the CDE from other networks, penetration tests are performed on segmentation controls as follows:
- At least once every six months and after any changes to segmentation controls/methods.
- Covering all segmentation controls/methods in use.
- According to the entity’s defined penetration testing methodology.
- Confirming that the segmentation controls/methods are operational and effective, and isolate the CDE from all out-of-scope systems.
- Confirming effectiveness of any use of isolation to separate systems with differing security levels (see Requirement 2.2.3).
- Performed by a qualified internal resource or qualified external third party.
- Organizational independence of the tester exists (not required to be a QSA or ASV).
controls.title: Penetration Test on Isolated CDE (Service Providers)

controls.body: Security awareness training includes awareness about the acceptable use of end-user technologies in accordance with Requirement 12.2.1.
controls.title: Awareness Training of Acceptable Use of End-User Technologies

controls.body: If a user session has been idle for more than 15 minutes, the user is required to re-authenticate to re-activate the terminal or session.
controls.title: User Idle Session

controls.body: Users, devices, and other assets are authenticated (i.e., single-factor, multi-factor) based on the risk of the transaction (i.e., individuals' security and privacy risks and other business-related risks).
controls.title: User Identification and Authentication

controls.body: The organization establishes, documents, implements, and maintains methods, processes and procedures to ensure the required level of continuity for information security during exceptional situations.
controls.title: Implementing Information Security Continuity

controls.body: The contractual agreements with employees and contractors state their and the organization’s responsibilities and commitment to comply with information security policies, as well as the consequences for misconduct.
controls.title: Compliance with Information Security Policies

controls.body: The organization has established a process for assigning and approving access rights and applying the minimum principle ("need to know"). Quarterly reviews are conducted on the assigned access rights and modified where applicable based on the review.
controls.title: Access Right Management

controls.body: A) Biometric and medical data storage shall be protected by at least the use of pseudonymisation or encryption techniques (or both).
controls.title: Pseudonymisation

controls.body: A supplier management process is in place, and management conducts annual risk assessments of potential and existing contractors and cooperation partners. Corrective actions are taken as needed based on the evaluation report.
controls.title: Contractors and Partners Risk Assessment

controls.body: All access to sensitive data must be logged to the extent technically possible and permitted by applicable laws and organizational policy.
controls.title: Access Logs of Sensitive Data

controls.body: The organization implements strong authentication (i.e., multi-factor authentication) for access to data of very high protection needs.
controls.title: User Authentication For Data of Very High Protection Needs

controls.body: The organization has implemented a change management process for changes to the organization, business processes and IT systems and outlines the information security requirements to prevent an uncontrolled reduction in information security.
controls.title: Change Management

controls.body: The organization has defined and implemented technical and organizational measures to protect against malware.
controls.title: Protection from Malware

controls.body: A Data Protection policy is established and communicated to employees and contractors within the organization. The policy is reviewed by management on an annual basis or in case of significant changes.
controls.title: Data Protection Policy

controls.body: Employees and project members are trained annually on the safe handling of vehicles, components and classified parts that require protection.
controls.title: Prototype Handling Awareness Training

controls.body: Contractor approvals and non-disclosure agreements with relevant subcontractors are in place, specifying minimum requirements to be met for the protection of prototypes.
controls.title: Subcontractors Requirements

controls.body: Affirmative consent is obtained and maintained from individuals prior to any processing of their sensitive personal information. Individuals are provided with a mechanism to withdraw their consent, and any such requests are documented and retained in accordance with organization policies.
controls.title: Consent on Processing of Sensitive Personal Information

controls.body: Unique user IDs and secure passwords are used for identification and authentication when accessing information and IT systems. Management conducts user access reviews at regular intervals to ensure that access is appropriately restricted and access is modified or removed in a timely manner based on the results of the review.
controls.title: Secure Access

controls.body: Each responsible entity shall verify at least once each calendar quarter that individuals with active electronic access or unescorted physical access have authorization records.
controls.title: Quarterly Verification of Authorization Records

controls.body:
Each responsible entity shall verify at least once every 15 calendar months that all user accounts, user account groups, or user
role categories and their specific, associated privileges are correct and are those that the responsible entity determines are necessary.
controls.title: Verification of Privileges

controls.body: Employees and contractors are required to complete information security and privacy awareness training as part of the onboarding process and annually thereafter.
controls.title: Awareness Training

controls.body:
Each responsible entity shall verify at least once every 15 calendar months that all individuals with provisioned access to BCSI:
6.2.1. Have an authorization record; and
6.2.2. Still need the provisioned access to perform their current work functions, as determined by the responsible entity.
controls.title: Verification of Electronic and Physical Access to BCSI

controls.body: A) The Applicant shall have a policy, rules or procedure in place to periodically train its personnel having permanent or regular access to personal data.
controls.title: Duty to Train Personnel on Data Protection

controls.body: The use of utility programs that can be capable of overriding system and application controls shall be restricted and tightly controlled.
controls.title: Use of Privileged Utility Programs (27017)

controls.body: A confidentiality or non-disclosure agreement (NDA) reflecting the organization`s needs for information protection is identified, documented, and signed by all parties with access to confidential information. Requirements regarding the use of non-disclosure agreements and the handling of sensitive information are reviewed on a regular basis.
controls.title: Non-disclosure Agreements

controls.body: The Applicant shall be able to explain the decisions made by the automated decision-making to the data subject.
controls.title: Rights to Explanations on the Decisions

controls.body: The organization's network is divided into multiple distinct zones with controlled and monitored access to detect or prevent unintended data exchange or access between IT systems.
controls.title: Network Segmentation

controls.body: The use of resources shall be monitored and adjusted in line with current and expected capacity requirements.
controls.title: Capacity Management (27017)

controls.body: Affirmative consent is obtained and maintained from individuals prior to any processing of their sensitive personal information. Individuals are provided with a mechanism to withdraw their consent, and any such requests are documented and retained in accordance with organization policies.
controls.title: Consent on Processing of Sensitive Personal Information
